rationale: CommandResponseFromJSON is also the decoder used by Client4.ExecuteCommand/ExecuteCommandWithTeam for server-emitted responses that are never run through IsValid server-side, so placing validation in the shared decoder is misplaced; the human thread asks for the same relocation of the call to commandWebhook/DoCommandRequest, albeit motivated by logger context rather than client breakage.
No table case puts a null element in extra_responses, so the nil-skip branch of IsValid (and the nested text-length branch) is exercised only by construction; a small but correct coverage gap.

len(o.Text) counts bytes against a hardcoded 65535 while Post.IsValid enforces a configurable rune count (PostMessageMaxRunesV2 / determineMaxPostSize), which is exactly the byte-vs-character concern the human thread raised.
The comment restates the condition; purely stylistic, no defect.
A considered-and-cleared note asserting no defect (the > 65535 vs 65536-byte test is indeed exact).
65535 is a function-local literal that duplicates PostMessageMaxBytesV2 rather than referencing it or a package constant, unlike the file's other constants; correct and actionable but small.
The only in_channel cases in TestCommandResponseFromJSON both expect errors; there is no success case pinning that in_channel is accepted by the new allowlist.
Cleared note: the *AppError is nil-tested as a concrete pointer before being returned as error, so no typed-nil escape.
TestCommandResponseFromHTTPBody has no case for an oversized or invalid text/plain body, so the plain-text path's non-validation is unpinned; a small test suggestion.

IsValid checks only ResponseType, Text length and recursion; ChannelId, Type, Username, IconURL, Props and Attachments (which have their own MessageAttachment.IsValid) are untouched, so the scope observation is accurate though largely a design/scope remark.
Only the 65536-byte rejection is tested; nothing pins that exactly 65535 bytes passes, so a >= regression would go unnoticed.

IsValid explicitly skips nil ExtraResponses entries, and HandleCommandResponse passes each entry to HandleCommandResponsePost which dereferences response.Type without a nil check, so {"extra_responses":[null]} from a custom command or command webhook reaches a nil-pointer panic; pre-existing, but the new validation is the natural place to reject it.
There is no TestCommandResponseIsValid; the exported method is only exercised through CommandResponseFromJSON, a small coverage/structure nit.

When io.ReadAll fails the function returns (nil, nil), discarding the error and forcing callers into a separate nil check that reports a generic 'empty response'; true but pre-existing and outside the changed hunk.
Considered-and-cleared note asserting the allowlist is fine; no defect claimed.
The nested error is returned verbatim with no index or path, so an integration author cannot tell which extra_responses entry failed; small debuggability gap.

One invalid nested entry (even at depth 2, which HandleCommandResponse never reads) rejects the entire payload with a hard error, contrasting with HandleCommandResponse's per-entry continue-and-log; this is a facet of the human thread's objection to hard-erroring instead of logging a warning.
Considered-and-cleared stack-exhaustion note; asserts no defect.
The asymmetry is real (stringification is one level deep, IsValid recurses), but nested ExtraResponses beyond one level are never consumed by HandleCommandResponse, so nothing observable follows.
DetailedError strings carry no offending value or actual/max length, unlike Post.IsValid which passes Length/MaxLength params; small debuggability nit.
Considered-and-cleared note that empty ResponseType is intentionally accepted; no defect.

commandWebhook is served through web.Handler which wraps r.Body in http.MaxBytesReader(MaximumPayloadSizeBytes) before the handler runs, so the body is already bounded; the implied unbounded-read concern does not hold (and is pre-existing regardless).

Calling IsValid inside the decoder turns previously tolerated payloads into hard failures at both ingest sites (500 in DoCommandRequest, 400 in commandWebhook) with no config gate — the same compatibility-break concern the human thread raised when asking for a logged warning instead of an error.
Whitespace preference only.

True that i18n-check omits `mmgotool i18n check`, but this is a repository-tooling observation outside the change under review rather than a defect in the PR; borderline, since it explains why the missing keys go uncaught.

CommandResponseFromPlainText never calls IsValid, so the text-length rule applies only to application/json bodies; a real inconsistency in the new validation, though the length is re-checked at post creation so practical impact is small.
Explicitly asserts no defect; test-data naming.
Considered-and-cleared nil-receiver note; sibling IsValid methods omit the guard too.
Space indentation inside a raw string literal in one test case; purely cosmetic and untouched by gofmt.
Self-described as not a bug; idiomatic if-scoped err.

grep of server/i18n/en.json finds no model.command_response.is_valid.* entries, so the raw id becomes the translated message; this is the human thread's request to run i18n-extract for the new error ids.
Notes a pre-existing table convention without asserting a defect.

The new ShouldError cases only assert.Error/assert.Nil and never check the AppError Id or StatusCode, so a case failing for an unrelated reason would still pass, and the ASCII payload cannot distinguish byte from rune counting; correct, actionable test-strength nit.

Accurate that both server call sites wrap the AppError in a fresh outer error with their own fixed status (500 / 400) and Client4 wraps in fmt.Errorf, but this is the existing convention for every model IsValid and offers no clear action for this change.
Sibling IsValid methods in the model package (Post, Command) also lack doc comments; stylistic preference, not a defect.

Same defect as the maintainer's "let's not throw a hard error, this might break existing servers" comment on that exact return: validation is welded into the decoder so callers cannot parse and then decide, and the fix (move it out of FromJSON) is what the thread asks for.

No cap on len(ExtraResponses) anywhere, and each entry becomes a post insert plus broadcast; the global 300KB payload cap (server/channels/web/handlers.go:213-216) bounds but does not eliminate the amplification. Pre-existing, and the strict-validation change is the natural place to bound it.
